judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the secretariat's summary of the H264-81 licensing declaration and contains the full RAND commitment, whose 'reasonable terms and conditions' and 'non-discriminatory basis' are the archetypal undefined standards, together with an unelaborated reciprocity condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the signed 2007 form (c033) and must be reconciled with the remark that H264-81 only supplied 'complementary information' to the 2003 H264-30 declaration (c028), which used the different 'will grant ... to use the patented material' wording (c003/c006).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Complementary information' is undefined and does not say whether the later statement adds to, amends or replaces H264-30, and the entry contains the obvious misspelling 'statment'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on whether the 2003 commitment (c003/c006) or the 2007 commitment (c027/c033) governs the same H.264 patents, and it uses different language from the parallel remarks for H264-91 and H264-101 ('updated information', c040/c051).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This declaration does not represent an actual grant of a license' is short and apparently clear, but 'actual grant' invites argument over whether it negates any binding obligation or merely defers the licence itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands in evident tension with the Option 2 promise to grant licences to an unrestricted number of applicants (c033) and with the reciprocity definition's 'shall only be required to license' (c036), which presupposes an enforceable licensing duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely administrative routing instructions keyed to document type; nothing here bears on obligations and nothing is genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'common text or twin text' box is consistent with the H.264 subject matter of the licensing declaration (c033); no conflict appears elsewhere in the compilation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is qualified by 'believes that it holds' and by the undefined essentiality test 'would be required to implement the above document', and it incorporates the unattached Common Patent Policy by reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the incorporated Common Patent Policy adds content to the checked Option 2 commitment (c033) and how that squares with the no-grant statement (c029) is a genuine whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This unchecked free-of-charge option contains an awkward internal structure (free of charge yet 'under other reasonable terms and conditions', plus a reservation to charge) but it was not selected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'check one box only' directs to Option 2 (c033), Option 1 is inoperative here, though the 'Free of charge' definition (c035) shows the drafters treated reasonable terms as separable from price.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the operative RAND commitment: 'prepared to grant', 'reasonable terms and conditions' and 'non-discriminatory basis' are all undefined, and it is silent on whether an initial offer must itself be reasonable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against 'Negotiations are left to the parties concerned and are performed outside the ITU-T' in its own text, against 'This declaration does not represent an actual grant of a license' (c029), and against the reciprocity definition (c036) — the classic set of provisions a court must harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The unwilling-to-license option is unchecked and its disclosure list is specific and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is mutually exclusive with the selected Option 2 (c033) and creates no tension with anything else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition explains 'free of charge' clearly enough but ends with an open-ended illustrative list of 'other reasonable terms and conditions such as those relating to governing law, field of use, reciprocity, warranties, etc.' — a catch-all whose reach is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Option 1 was not selected (c032), this definition is on its face inapplicable, yet its list of what 'reasonable terms and conditions' may include would be pressed as a guide to the identical phrase in the operative Option 2 (c033).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reciprocity definition is drafted as a limit on the Patent Holder's duty but leaves 'commit to license' undefined and does not say what happens if a prospective licensee refuses — only that the holder is not 'required' to license.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reciprocity was marked in the operative Option 2 (c033), and this 2007 wording differs from the 2003 definition (c005), so the two declarations covering the same H.264 patents carry differently phrased conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line cross-reference note applicable only to option 3; there is nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Option 3 was not selected (c034), so the note is inert and consistent with the rest of the form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical inert note on the duplicate form; wholly mechanical and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Like c037 it depends on an unselected option (c034) and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The H264-91 summary reproduces the full RAND commitment, resting on the undefined 'reasonable terms and conditions' and 'non-discriminatory basis' and the unelaborated reciprocity condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the database rendering of the signed 2008 form (c033) and, per the remark (c040), 'updates' the 2003 declaration (c006) whose wording differed, leaving open which text controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Updated information relative to their earlier statement' does not say whether the earlier declaration is amended, supplemented or superseded; the ambiguity is in 'updated'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs the relation between the 2003 declaration (c003/c006) and the 2007-form declaration (c033/c039), and differs from the 'complementary information' formulation used for H264-81 (c028).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single line 'does not represent an actual grant of a license' is terse, and 'actual grant' can be read either as denying any binding effect or merely as saying no licence issues automatically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against the Option 2 undertaking in the same form (c045) and against the reciprocity definition's assumption that the holder can be 'required to license' (c048).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Routing and document-type instructions only; the marked 'common text or twin text' box carries no substantive obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the H.264 subject matter identified in the same form and with the earlier declarations (c030).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is materially corrupted — 'ba to a eine the above docuynent and pereby declares, in accordance with the Common Patent Policy for weynsere' — so the standard incorporated and the scope of the declaration cannot be read off the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its intelligible counterpart in the earlier form (c031) supplies the missing reference to the Common Patent Policy, but the reader must go outside this provision to find it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The free-of-charge option was not marked; it carries the same 'other reasonable terms and conditions' tension as its 2007 analogue but has no operative role.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Option 2 was the option selected in this form (c045/c050), so Option 1 does not operate and does not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 2010 RAND commitment turns on the undefined 'reasonable terms and conditions' and 'non-discriminatory basis', and 'is prepared to grant' invites argument over whether it is a promise or a statement of willingness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As reproduced, the reciprocity box shows no mark ('Also mark here if...'), yet the corresponding database entry (c050) states the willingness is conditioned on reciprocity — and the provision must also be squared with 'does not represent an actual grant of a license' (c041) and 'Negotiations are left to the parties concerned'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The unwilling option is unmarked and its enumerated disclosure requirements are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is mutually exclusive with the selected Option 2 (c045) and raises no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is reasonably clear on monetary compensation but closes with an open-ended 'such as those relating to governing law, field of use, reciprocity, warranties, etc.', a catch-all of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Option 1 was not marked (c044), so the definition is nominally inapplicable, yet it defines the very phrase used in the operative Option 2 (c045) and would be invoked to colour it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines reciprocity only negatively ('shall only be required to license ... if'), leaving the consequence of a licensee's refusal and the meaning of 'commit to license' unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs in terms from the 2003 reciprocity definition (c005) applying to the same H.264 patents, and it presupposes an enforceable duty to license that the no-grant statement (c041) appears to disclaim.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cross-referencing note tied to an unselected option; there is nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Option 3 was not marked (c046), so the note is inert and consistent with the form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The H264-101 summary states the full RAND commitment, whose 'reasonable terms and conditions' and 'non-discriminatory basis' are undefined, and asserts a reciprocity condition without stating its effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that willingness 'is conditioned on reciprocity' although the reciprocity box in the signed 2010 form (c045) appears unmarked, and it sits beneath the secretariat disclaimer that the database is not certified accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Updated information relative to their earlier statement' leaves unclear whether the earlier declarations are supplemented or replaced, and the entry contains obvious errors ('in in', '2008-1 1-3').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the link between the 2003, 2008 and 2010 declarations (c006, c039, c050) made by two different corporate entities, and elsewhere the same compilation misdescribes the cross-reference as 'H262-101', so the succession of commitments is not cleanly stated.
